slides.hint: Think of the tiger, terrapin and hornbill.
slides.notes: Hands up / choral True-True-False, 6 min max. Elicit each verdict BEFORE tapping Next step. Say the why orally: terrapins are endangered; forests gone means homes gone; eco means safe. Misconception: eco-friendly misread as harmful (cf. Module p.35 Q4 False). Follow-up: ask what poaching means (one word: illegal hunting). Bridge: same skill today — match the right sentence. Retrieval from 2026-09-14 deck only; do not reteach p.34.

slides.prompt: Say it. Know it. Repeat after me.
slides.notes: Teacher models each once, pupils repeat twice; drill the stressed caps syllable. Both words verified non-A2 (0 matches, A2 Key Aug 2025). Keep Malay brief; examples are paraphrases, not book verbatim.
Correct poacher = illegal hunter (not any hunter). Cue the deforestation/conservation swap early: de-FOR-est = forest gone; con-SERVE = save. Both words verified non-A2.

slides.hint: Person, forest, danger, help — point to each.
slides.notes: Required synthesis beat: all four taught words together on one slide, final state complete, no new teaching. Build with Next step; pupils give the Malay before each appears where possible. Say the swap cue orally: de-FOR-est means forest gone; con-SERVE means save. 4 min. Steps form chosen over reveal so the 96px prompt-only scale cannot overflow.

slides.prompt: Read The Light Bulb on page 36. Gaps 1 to 4. Listen and follow.
slides.hint: credited — people say he did it. Practical — useful, works well. Power station — makes electricity.
slides.notes: Display route: project the module PDF / pupils open p.36 — full passage is read from the book, not reprinted here. Teacher reads once at natural speed, then gap sentences slowly; choral repeat trial and error + power station. Defer solving: just follow first. Pronunciation: credited KREE-dit-ed, practical PRAK-ti-kel. credited/practical verified non-A2; station is A2 (record 1421).

slides.feedback: Each sentence fits before and after its gap.
slides.notes: New matrix pair-matching game, first half. Tap one sentence per gap, then Reveal. Neutral attempt until Reveal; wrong rows show Not yet, canonical rows show Correct + clue. Gap 2 easiest (numbers); Gap 1 hardest (Although contrast). Misconception: matching one shared word — cue read before AND after the gap. 4 min.

slides.feedback: Street light everywhere, then the big ending.
slides.notes: Matrix second half. All four sentences stay visible so pupils choose from the full set. Reset clears this half only. 4 min.

slides.feedback: Although joins ideas. 3,000 tries. Homes and streets. Big ending.
slides.notes: Keys-only beat by teacher request. Pupils copy keys quietly, 3 min. Redirect A-for-1 attempts to the Although contrast. No new vocabulary here.

slides.prompt: Read Teleportation on page 37. Listen and follow.
slides.hint: crisis — a bad emergency. Evacuate — move people to safety. Pollution — dirty air.
slides.notes: Same display route from the book, faster cycle (6 min). Choral repeat evacuate + pollution. Correct teleportation = fast travel, same time (not time travel). crisis/evacuate/pollution verified non-A2; invention and electricity are A2 (records 794, 481).

slides.feedback: Family visits fast, rescue moves faster.
slides.notes: Second matrix round, higher independence, first half (4 min). Watch the 6/H vs 7/F swap later — cue: 6 = move fast, 7 = clean air. Reset clears this half only.

slides.feedback: Clean air first, then the ending.
slides.notes: Matrix last half (3 min). Gap 8 easiest (in conclusion = ending). All four sentences stay visible.

slides.feedback: Family plus emergency. Move out fast. Clean air. Ending.
slides.notes: Keys-only beat. Pupils record keys; quick choral read of the four clue phrases. 3 min.

slides.prompt: Light Bulb: why 3,000? Which place helped?
slides.hint: 1 = wanted it to work. 2 = New York homes.
slides.answer: 1. He tried until it worked. 2. Homes or streets.
slides.feedback: Trying many times is trial and error.
slides.notes: Fresh comprehension, not module items. Individual books, short answers of 8 words or fewer; copying whole gap sentences is not accepted. 4 min for both.

slides.hint: Crisis saves lives. Planet means clean air.
slides.answer: Crisis: move people out fast. Planet: less pollution.
slides.notes: Fresh comprehension, not module items. Short answers of 8 words or fewer; copying whole gap sentences is not accepted.

slides.prompt: Bulb or teleportation for you? Why?
slides.notes: Open view question: accept any intelligible reason, e.g. Bulb — I study at night; Teleportation — visit family fast. Hands check if time allows, else drop discussion when behind.

slides.hint: Today: page 35 Q5 to Q8, pages 36 to 37 keys. Finish at home.
items: A: He tried over three thousand designs.
